# Changelog

## 0.1.0 (unreleased)

- First version: Rack middleware and Rails helpers that add eLLMo content (cached, refreshed in the background) and report page views from a background thread in gzipped batches (`source: "rails-sdk"`).
- Checks this client's switches (`GET analytics-v2.tryellmo.com/access/<client id>`, every 30 min per process, in the background): page views off discards them, content off serves and fetches none. One failed check is skipped; two in a row count as off.
- `config.debug` (or `ELLMO_DEBUG=1`): logs every call to eLLMo and its answer, prefixed `[ellmo-ai http]`; page-view uploads logged decoded and in full. `config.debug_body_limit` / `ELLMO_DEBUG_BODY` caps logged answers (2000 characters).
- Supports Rails 6.1+. Before Rails 7.1, Rails response bodies can't be read with `to_ary` (6.1 returns nil, 7.0 doesn't define it), so the middleware reads buffered ones itself and leaves streamed ones (`ActionController::Live`, `stream: true`) alone. On Rack 2 the visitor cookie is written as `Set-Cookie`, next to the app's own cookies.
- Page views carry the status the visitor got: `EllmoAi::FinalStatus`, installed outermost by the Railtie, reports after `Rack::ConditionalGet` has turned a current page into a `304`. A `304` from the controller (`fresh_when` / `stale?`) is counted too, unless the request asked for something other than HTML.
- `config.hide_other_json_ld` (default `false`): tags eLLMo's JSON-LD `data-ellmo-schema` and adds a small inline script that sets `type="application/ld+json+hidden"` on the page's other JSON-LD, only when eLLMo's is present. Works through the middleware and the `ellmo_structured` helper; uses the request's CSP nonce when the app sets a nonce generator.
- Robustness (code review): response bodies are always closed (Rack 2 and Rails' `to_ary` don't close); content goes before the page's own `</head>` / after its own `<body>`, never one in a comment, script, style or template, and `<body>` attributes containing `>` stay whole; pages in another charset are left alone; installing the middleware twice adds content once; content is looked up only for requests that take HTML, and "no content" results aren't kept past their freshness; values that aren't valid UTF-8 are repaired instead of losing the batch, a receiver `4xx` is dropped (not retried, not counted as sent), and an error never stops the reporter thread; the first page waits `cold_wait` in total, not twice; until eLLMo has answered the access check, a timed-out lookup doesn't fall back to a shared cache, and an API refusal (`4xx`) drops what was cached; numeric settings that aren't usable fall back to their defaults; no visitor cookie on publicly cacheable responses or while page views are off; malformed visitor cookies are replaced; the view helpers never raise; fork- and thread-safety for in-flight refreshes, the first access check and the first use of the store and reporter.
- Privacy and several sites: the visitor's `Cookie` header is no longer sent to eLLMo (`config.forward_cookies = true` to send it); `config.visitor_cookie` takes a callable (consent); `config.client_id` takes a callable of the request, with a content cache and switches per client; only paths ending in a file type are skipped (`/users/jane.doe` is a page).
- Rails' health check (`rails/health#show`, `/up` since Rails 7.1) gets no content and isn't counted as a page view: load balancers and uptime monitors call it every few seconds.
- Needs the `embedded-content_v2` function (the same one `ellmo-ai-react` 1.0 uses) to be deployed; until then pages render unchanged.
